motion: The Constitutional Right to Bear Arms Has Outlived its Usefulness

dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: Consider a lone resident facing an armed intruder while emergency help is minutes away. A lawful firearm can prevent immediate harm. That example shows the right still performs a vital protective role.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Welcome. The motion is that the Constitutional Right to Bear Arms Has Outlived its Usefulness. Hina argues for it, and Angus argues against it. Each gets thirty seconds to open, followed by two and a half minutes of crossfire, then thirty-second closings, with a ten-second cue.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: A constitutional right created for muskets cannot govern weapons that fire rapidly and cause mass harm. We can respect lawful self-defense while replacing an outdated guarantee with focused safety rules. The motion is true because public protection now requires flexibility.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Now his summation against the motion, Angus.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: The right remains useful because it protects people when institutions fail. A family facing immediate violence cannot wait for perfect policy or guaranteed official help. Lawful ownership also lets citizens defend themselves and resist abuse. The answer is responsible regulation, not abandoning a liberty that still matters.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Ten seconds please.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: You treat every gun as proof the right has failed, but misuse does not erase proper use. We can punish violence, improve training, and keep self-defense available. Removing the right would leave peaceful citizens-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: I'm sorry. Your time is up. Thank you very much.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: As the conversation continues, we're going to give you each a chance to rebut one another. It runs two and a half minutes, starting the moment I stop. Go.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Imagine a legally purchased rifle used in a crowded public place within seconds. Existing safeguards may not prevent that harm. It shows the constitutional protection can block timely safety measures, which is why its usefulness has expired.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I believe armed citizens always make us safer. The right preserves a final defense when police cannot arrive, so its usefulness cannot be judged only by criminal misuse.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Your weakest point is that ownership automatically supplies safety. A weapon may help one person, but widespread access also makes panic, accidents, and impulsive violence more dangerous; that tradeoff defeats your claim.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: In a school, unarmed guards make us safer. That specific setting calls for a different protective choice, while the broader right still protects citizens elsewhere.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: One moment you're saying i believe armed citizens always make us safer, then you're having them in a school, unarmed guards make us safer. Which?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: They fit by recognizing that safety depends on circumstances, not one mechanical answer. I still believe armed citizens always make us safer as a general safeguard, while this school case favors unarmed guards for its particular risks.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: When a weapon can harm many people rapidly in a confined public space, the government should be able to restrict access. Under that condition, the old right has outlived its usefulness.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Training standards deserve attention, and schools need careful emergency plans. But those details do not answer the central question: citizens still need a protected means of defense, so the right remains useful.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: A right that blocks effective safety rules has outlived its usefulness wherever public danger is substantial. Its broad constitutional shield is the problem, even when individual cases deserve careful treatment.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: If your broad claim covers substantial danger, why preserve any protected right at all? Your careful exceptions cannot repair a principle that lets officials decide liberty disappears whenever fear rises.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: No, my claim does not erase every individual choice; it rejects the premise that constitutional protection must control every case. Officials should be able to act when weapons create shared danger, which is why reform is necessary.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I grant that dangerous weapons require firm rules. But your main point gives officials power to redefine danger broadly, and that risks peaceful citizens' protection; the constitutional right remains useful as a limit on that power.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: That limit is the point I reject. Calling the right a safeguard does not justify keeping language that prevents modern solutions; adaptable rules protect people better than an old guarantee.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Ten.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Time. I'm going to jump in because we're going to go to closing statements. Now we move on to our final round. Hina, you are up first.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: The amendment was designed for an old danger, but today's weapons multiply harm quickly. Keeping it unchanged protects a symbol, not public safety, because

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Let me make one quick point: removing-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Angus, hold on. Let Hina finish, please.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: because public safety requires rules that can change as weapons change. A permanent barrier to those rules is no longer useful, even if self-defense remains legitimate.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: You have ten seconds left.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: We can preserve self-defense without preserving an outdated constitutional obstacle.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: You can come in, Angus.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: This right is not obsolete because the need for self-defense has not vanished. People still face immediate threats, and officials cannot promise instant protection. Keep the right, regulate misuse, and preserve a vital safeguard for ordinary citizens.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Thank you both for a thoughtful debate. That concludes our discussion, and we appreciate your attention.
